rules.problem: DANGER: You are about to pay a deposit without a signed contract. This is how most international students lose their money in Korea. No contract = no legal protection.
action: STOP. Do not send any money.
Demand written contract (임대차계약서) BEFORE any payment
Verify landlord owns the property: iros.go.kr, costs only 700 won
After signing: go to 주민센터 within 14 days for 전입신고 and 확정일자
Call 1345 for free legal advice in English

rules.problem: Rental fraud (전세 사기) is extremely common in Korea. Prices too cheap compared to nearby places = major red flag.
action: Check market price on land.naver.com or Zigbang app
If price is 20%+ below market rate, be very suspicious
Always check 등기부등본 (property registry) at iros.go.kr
Never rush into signing — legitimate landlords won't pressure you

rules.problem: Without 전입신고 and 확정일자, you have zero legal protection for your deposit.
action: Go to nearest 주민센터 within 14 days of moving in
Bring: passport, ARC, signed lease contract
Request 전입신고 (free) AND 확정일자 (600 won)
Can also be done online at government24.go.kr

rules.problem: 고시원 rooms are very small (3-7 sqm). Good for short stays but check fire safety.
action: Check for fire sprinklers and emergency exit signs
Ask if meals are included — some offer free rice and kimchi
Typical cost: 300,000-500,000 won/month with utilities
Not recommended for stays longer than 3 months (mental health impact)

rules.problem: Mold and maintenance issues are common in Korean housing. Landlord is legally required to fix structural issues.
action: Take photos of all defects on move-in day immediately
Tell landlord via KakaoTalk or text to create a written record
Boiler (보일러) breaking in winter = urgent. Escalate immediately.
If landlord refuses: contact 주택임대차분쟁조정위원회 (housing dispute committee)
